gaps.text: In-line measurement of Broth temperature with temperature sensor in the broth

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Low-level fusion of the per-method blocks, with block scaling so that no method dominates the model. All probes must look at the same port and be synchronised to a common time step, and each block keeps its own calibration and diagnostics. The fused model must beat the best single method on held-out runs, otherwise the extra methods are dropped.)
No supplied source names specific reference methods or sampling frequencies for yeast fermentation (for example dry cell weight, viable counts, or an HPLC method for metabolites).
No supplied source gives detection limits, accuracy or response times for these methods in fermentation broth.

items.finding: The source says temperature sensitivity of OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solutions in NIR and MIR, making tempered sample holders necessary.
items.how_it_applies: This could justify including temperature monitoring or control in the feasibility study, but it does not demonstrate an in-broth temperature sensor.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The statement concerns NIR/MIR aqueous measurements with tempered sample holders, not UV-Vis or Raman in fermentation broth, and it is not evidence for an in-line broth temperature probe.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
citation.label: E03 ¶12

items.finding: Low-level data fusion is described as the simplest way to combine inputs by rearranging variables from different sources into a new data matrix.
items.how_it_applies: This supports trying a low-level fusion design with per-method blocks, while still requiring held-out testing to see whether fusion beats the best single method.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This is a review statement, not a fermentation study, and it does not address block scaling, probe synchronisation, or calibration diagnostics for the proposed spectroscopy setup.

citation.quote: Low-level data fusion (LLDF) is considered the simplest method to achieve a combination of inputs. In this case, the data is rearranged into a new data matrix, where the variables coming from different sources are placed one after the other.
citation.label: E01 ¶31

items.finding: The source states that before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate each dataset's contribution to the model and its complementarity.
items.how_it_applies: This supports assessing each spectroscopy block and dropping extra methods if the fused model does not outperform the best single method on held-out runs.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The statement is general and does not provide fermentation-specific evidence, nor does it define how to scale blocks or synchronise probes.

citation.quote: Before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate the contribution of each dataset to the model and its complementarity.
citation.label: E01 ¶82
